For an octahedral $d^3$ complex, the spin-allowed transitions from the $^4A_{2g}$ ground state are to the $^4T_{2g}$, $^4T_{1g}(F)$, and $^4T_{1g}(P)$ states. The energy of the lowest spin-allowed transition is given by:
$$\nu_1 = 10Dq = 17,430 \text{ cm}^{-1}$$
Thus, the ligand-field splitting parameter is:
$$Dq = 1,743 \text{ cm}^{-1}$$

The positions of the other spin-allowed bands ($\nu_2 = 25,000 \text{ cm}^{-1}$ and $\nu_3 = 39,000 \text{ cm}^{-1}$) depend on both $Dq$ and the Racah parameter $B$. Using a Tanabe-Sugano fit (or the ratio method), these values yield a Racah parameter $B$:
$$B \approx 780.7 \text{ cm}^{-1}$$

The lowest-energy spin-forbidden transition in a $d^3$ octahedral complex is the transition to the $^2E_g$ state. Unlike the spin-allowed states, the energy of the $^2E_g$ state is relatively independent of $Dq$ but depends on both $B$ and the Racah parameter $C$. By computing the energy of the $^2E_g$ state for the determined $Dq$ and $B$, and fitting it to the observed value of $15,410 \text{ cm}^{-1}$:
$$\nu(^2E_g) = 15,410 \text{ cm}^{-1} \implies C \approx 3,243 \text{ cm}^{-1}$$

- $Dq = 1,743 \text{ cm}^{-1}$
- $B = 780.7 \text{ cm}^{-1}$
- $C = 3,243 \text{ cm}^{-1}$
